title: Announcing the Dungeon Dive Patreon
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YOe2PL-1gT0

Daniel (@dungeondive) launches the Dungeon Dive Patreon, and spends almost the entire video explaining why — opening with an acknowledgement that some viewers will already be rolling their eyes, because there are a lot of Patreons out there.

The reasoning amounts to a statement of what the channel refuses to be. Daniel will not run advertisements: making a video about a game that people then go and buy is already a form of advertising, and he has no interest in subjecting viewers to intrusive mid-rolls for products with nothing to do with the hobby. If YouTube ever forces ads onto every channel, he says, he will likely stop or move platforms. He will not take paid Kickstarter promotions, and has already turned some down — the three previews he has done were ones he sought out himself, for small projects he wanted to see succeed. He also wants to limit review copies, to avoid becoming another instrument of a publisher's marketing department.

The Patreon is how the channel funds new material without any of that. Two tiers at three and five dollars, with written pieces and photo essays, periodic giveaways and quarterly video meet-ups; nothing currently free moves behind a paywall. One patron in Korea had already found it before Daniel announced it to anybody.

----

No ads, no paid previews, limited review copies. How much of a channel's independence is actually visible from the outside — and would you notice if it quietly went?
